profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary: Currently pursuing a master degree in software engineering with a focus on cloud computing and virtualization at San Jose State University. Expected graduation date is May 2022. My roles involved building full stack web application. Some of my hobbies include gardening, exercising and chasing my dog in the backyard.

positions.title: Computer Science Intern
positions.description:
Lead the development of data visualization for the metallurgical internal tool to assist metallurgical engineers on creating custom trend data.
• The tech stack includes Angular and RxJs for the frontend, GraphQl for api, ASP.NET core for the backend and MySQL for the database.
• Implemented line graph for trending data and historical table for viewing past data. 
• Improved efficiency by 80% with the tool replacing excel and allowing users to create custom trend graphs.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Designed and implemented a cloud-based security policy management software called FortiPortal that allows customers to manage Fortinet’s products
• Tech stack includes React for the frontend, RESTful APIs, Spring Framework for the backend and MySQL for the database
• Broke down frontend codebase into reusable components, improving readability and allowing easier maintenance
• Collaborated with FortiPortal product manager for customer specs, tradeoffs, timelines, and converted the business requirements into technical requirements
• Drove the frontend effort for an automatic form generator to create forms based on syntax from the backend, using a JSON format structure that contains metadata on the form structure.
• Decreased frontend codebase by 30%, avoiding unnecessary code addition when introducing new forms  

Created automation tools that helps simplify QA and test engineers workflow
• Lead the frontend effort for the user interface part of the automation tool
• Tech stack is using Vue for the frontend,  Django for the backend, RESTful api and MySQL for the backend
• Interface allows users to monitor test case status and access the command line interface of Fortinet network products

positions.title: Software Intern
positions.description:
Worked on custom websites for clients of the company
• Tech stack includes Django template for frontend development and python for backend work.
• Discussed with clients on business requirements and converting them to technical requirements.

positions.title: Engineering Co-op/Intern
positions.description:
Worked on both the C919 and B737 project at GE Aviation in the Navigation and Guidance group. 
On the C919 project, I worked on the development of the navigation component of the flight management system (FMS). 
For the B737 project, I worked on testing and documenting different tools of the navigation component of the FMS.

positions.title: Bioinformatics Assistant
positions.description: Analyzed and filed microarray chip results with R language, MATLAB and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis.

volunteerExperiences.description: Comforted and acclimated the kids ages 6 - 10 with respiratory problems to the hospital setting

projects.title: Steam Reviews Sentiment Analysis Classifier
projects.description:
Developed a classification tool that takes in game reviews from a website called Steam and predicts if the reviewer is more likely to recommend the game. 
Used and compared results from several algorithms to determine the sentiment analysis of the reviews.

projects.title: Smart Supply Chain Management
projects.description: Lead the frontend app development for a Smart Supply Chain. Tech stack includes React for the frontend, Cordova for mobile conversion, NodeJs for the backend and MongoDB for the database. The app provides a map view of all deployed IoT warehouses for each user. App also displays individual warehouse details where users can view statistics on the sensors deployed in a warehouse. The sensors include temperature, humidity and UV sensors. The app will display a line graph for each sensor showing past sensor data.
